q: Furstenberg's correspondence principle (1977) translates combinatorial density results to ergodic theory. It states that for a set A ⊆ ℤ with upper density d̄(A) > 0, there exists a measure-preserving system (X,μ,T) and a set Ã ⊆ X with μ(Ã) = d̄(A) such that:
opts: A contains arbitrarily long arithmetic progressions iff Ã has the same property
A is syndetic iff Ã is T-invariant
exp: Furstenberg's principle: d̄(A∩(A-n)∩…∩(A-kn)) ≥ μ(Ã∩T⁻ⁿÃ∩…∩T⁻ᵏⁿÃ) − ε for most n. Multiple recurrence (positivity of the right side for some n) translates back to arithmetic progressions in A—this is the ergodic proof of Szemerédi's theorem.
